disclaimer: DEMONSTRATION RULES ONLY. These are generic examples for Packmate v2 and are not airline-specific. Actual baggage policies vary by airline, route, ticket class, and local regulations. Always verify with your carrier before travelling.
general_rules: Demo rule: cabin baggage is typically limited to about 8 kg and must fit in the overhead bin or under the seat.
Demo rule: checked baggage is commonly limited to about 23 kg per piece, subject to airline policy.
Demo rule: one personal item plus one cabin bag is a frequent allowance, but limits differ by airline.

rules.title: Liquids in cabin baggage
warnings: Demo rule: liquids in cabin baggage must be in containers of 100 ml or less, all fitting in one transparent resealable bag (max 1 L).

rules.title: Liquid containers above 100 ml in cabin
warnings: Demo rule: liquid containers above 100 ml are generally not permitted in cabin baggage unless medically required and documented.

rules.title: Sharp objects
warnings: Demo rule: sharp objects such as knives, large scissors, or razor blades are usually prohibited in cabin baggage and should be placed in checked baggage if allowed.

rules.title: External batteries and power banks
warnings: Demo rule: spare lithium batteries and power banks must normally be carried in cabin baggage, not checked baggage.
Demo rule: power banks above typical airline watt-hour limits may be refused; check your carrier's limit.
unknown_warnings: Demo rule: spare lithium batteries and power banks are subject to airline safety restrictions; confirm allowed placement with your carrier.
Demo rule: power banks above typical airline watt-hour limits may be refused; check your carrier's limit.

rules.title: Medications
warnings: Demo rule: essential medications should be kept in cabin baggage with supporting documentation when required.
Demo rule: liquid medications may exceed the 100 ml cabin limit when medically necessary, subject to airline approval.
unknown_warnings: Demo rule: essential medications may require supporting documentation; verify transport rules with your airline.

rules.title: Large liquids in checked baggage
warnings: Demo rule: larger liquid containers are generally more suitable for checked baggage, subject to weight and spill-safe packaging.
